summary: Curry County lookout first built in 1936, wrecked by wind in late 1941, replaced by a 14x14 cab in 1952 that was later converted to a radio building.

facts.design: 14 x 14 Amort-style ground lookout house built 1952 (current); the 1936 original was a 10-ft L-4 tower
facts.status_note: The 1952 cab was converted to an enclosed radio building (firelookout.com); the pages read do not show it still in lookout use
facts.agency: Coos Forest Protection Association (NHLR); firelookout.com calls the cab an Oregon Department of Forestry cab

events.note: Original 10-ft L-4 tower; firelookout.com gives 1936, and a June 1937 paper says it was built the previous fall; NHLR gives 1937
M.S. Brainard of Gold Beach assigned to the station; recalled after a few days when rain eased fire danger
Lookout reported a small boat adrift in heavy seas; a Coast Guard rescue followed
High winds destroyed the station in December 1941 per a Dec 17, 1941 paper and a Feb 1942 article; NHLR says 1942 storm; a March 1942 article says 'last January'
Site served as an Aircraft Warning Service post; activated March 9, 1942 (Roseburg Filter Center)
Emmett Freeman stationed there while the lookout was used as an air-raid warning point (February 1942 account)
Current 14x14 Amort-style lookout house; 1952 ODF annual report gives $810 labor and $878.33 materials; one mile of new road
10x10 concrete block building added for radio and microwave equipment

corrections.why: NHLR describes the current structure as a 14 x 14 Amort style lookout house built in 1952; the L-4 design was the 10-ft tower established in 1936.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the original lookout to 1937; firelookout.com gives 1936 and a June 1937 newspaper says it was built the previous fall, so 1936 is the better-supported date.

NHLR names the Coos Forest Protection Association as administrator; firelookout.com names the Oregon Department of Forestry for the cab and the Forest Lookouts page header names Coos FPA. The sources read do not settle who holds the site today.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: distance from Gold Beach (about five miles in 1937, about four miles east in 1942, two miles southeast on firelookout.com). Storm date: December 1941 per a Dec 17, 1941 paper and a Feb 1942 article, 1942 per NHLR, 'last January' per a March 1942 article. Current status: the cab was converted to a radio building per firelookout.com (undated); no source read says whether it is open, staffed or rentable, so access is left out. Staffing after 1941 is thin: a February 1942 account names Emmett Freeman as stationed there during air-raid warning use; no other staffing after 1941 was found in the pages read, apart from a 1966 Forest Service lookout report whose site name is garbled in the source. Record kind 'ground' and elevation 710.8 m fit the current structure.
